notes: Starter milestones for each stage. A founder can keep, edit or ignore them; `when` limits a suggestion to people it applies to.

templates.title: Talk to 10 people who have the problem
templates.why: Programs and investors at this stage all ask what you learned from real customers.

templates.title: Write the problem and who has it in two sentences
templates.why: If you can say it in two sentences, you can fit any application form.

templates.title: List what people use today instead, and why it falls short
templates.why: Shows you know the competition and gives you your reason to exist.

templates.title: Sketch the smallest version you could build in 8 weeks
templates.why: A small first version is what lets you reach the prototype stage.

templates.title: Find one advisor who has built something similar
templates.why: You asked for mentorship, and one good advisor saves months.

templates.title: Join a founder community near you
templates.why: You asked for a network, and peers are where first introductions come from.

templates.title: Look at programs for young or student founders
templates.why: Several programs only take founders under 30 or in school.

templates.title: Build a working prototype
templates.why: Most accelerators want to see something that works, even if it is rough.

templates.title: Put it in front of 5 real users and write down what they say
templates.why: User feedback is the main thing a prototype-stage program looks for.

templates.title: Decide what you will charge and test it with three people
templates.why: A price you have tested beats a guess on every application.

templates.title: Incorporate your company
templates.why: Most grants and loans need an incorporated company.

templates.title: Write a one-page summary of what you are building
templates.why: One page is what every intake form and intro email ends up needing.

templates.title: Apply to an incubator or accelerator that matches you
templates.why: You asked for mentorship or a network, and these give you both.

templates.title: Get your first paying customer
templates.why: Revenue is the clearest proof you are past the idea.

templates.title: Open a business bank account and start bookkeeping
templates.why: Funders ask for clean records, and it is hard to rebuild them later.

templates.title: Register for GST/HST once your sales pass $30,000 in four quarters
templates.why: Canada requires small businesses to register after that point.

templates.title: Pick the three numbers you will track every month
templates.why: Users, revenue and how many come back are what funders ask for first.

templates.title: Protect your name and what you built
templates.why: You asked about IP, and a trademark or filing is cheapest early.

templates.title: Apply for funding you match
templates.why: You asked for funding, and some programs are open to you now.

templates.title: Reach revenue you can count on each month
templates.why: Repeatable revenue is what moves you from earning to growing.

templates.title: Write a 12-month plan and budget
templates.why: Lenders and investors ask for it, and it keeps you honest.

templates.title: Check whether you can claim SR&ED for your technical work
templates.why: You asked for R&D support, and SR&ED returns part of what you spend.

templates.title: Pick your first export market and what it needs
templates.why: You asked for export help, and export programs ask for a target market.

templates.title: Hire or contract your first help
templates.why: You asked for talent, and it is the first thing that frees up your time.

templates.title: Line up funding for the next 12 months
templates.why: You asked for funding, and it takes months from start to cash.

templates.title: Set up payroll and CRA remittances before your first hire
templates.why: Missing remittances cause penalties that are easy to avoid.

templates.title: Name the next three hires and what each one unlocks
templates.why: Growth is usually limited by people, not by ideas.

templates.title: Open a second market or sales channel
templates.why: One channel is a risk, and funders look for a second.

templates.title: Decide how to fund growth: investors, debt or revenue
templates.why: You asked for funding, and each route changes who you talk to.

templates.title: Set a monthly update for your advisors or board
templates.why: A regular update keeps support coming when you need it.

templates.title: Protect what you have built before you expand
templates.why: You asked about IP, and expanding without it is the costly time to start.

templates.title: Mentor one earlier-stage founder
templates.why: Giving back builds your network and sharpens your own thinking.
